curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42101-1-1.pdf (one book, 48 pages; the buggy is steps 1-36, pages 4-44)

functions.does: The 12 tooth gear on top of the upright axle behind the seat steers the front wheels: turning it swings a white 2-long arm at the axle's foot, which pulls a link to the tie-rod beam joining the two steering knuckles.
functions.source: book: step 9 (the upright axle on its white arm), steps 19-20 (the knuckles), steps 21-22 (link and tie rod), step 27 (the axle and gear on top)

functions.does: The rear wheels ride on a swinging arm: the arm pivots under the seat and carries the 9-long rear axle, and the shock absorber runs from the frame behind the seat down to the arm's back, so the rear wheels rise and fall together.
functions.source: book: step 10 (the swinging arm), step 12 (the shock absorber, arrow), steps 14 and 23-24 (rear axle and wheels)
functions.note: how far the arm can swing is set by the shock absorber's travel; the shock's cylinder swings a little on its top pin as the arm moves

functions.does: The shock absorber's spring pushes the rear wheels back down.
functions.skip: a spring only matters under gravity or force

functions.does: The four wheels roll freely; there's no drive and no engine. The two rear wheels turn together on one 9-long axle; each front wheel turns on its own 3-long axle in its steering knuckle.
The steering wheel in front of the seat spins on its half pin; it isn't joined to the steering.
functions.source: inferred: steps 5 and 25 show it on a half pin in a pin with a cross hole, with nothing behind it; the book draws no arrow for it
